_comment: Loan-success-score component weights, per position. Unlike data/score_weights.json (permanent transfers), there's no value_for_money or resale_profit component: most loans carry no real fee (the packaged fee is 0 even when a real loan fee was agreed - see fetch_transfer_types.py), and a loan doesn't end in a sale of its own. playing_time is weighted heavily across every position - whether the loan actually delivered game time is usually the central question a loan gets judged on, independent of how well the player performed when they did play. value_growth is deliberately FLAT across every position (0.12) for the same reason as data/score_weights.json's flat value_growth/value_for_money: it's a single global percentile rank with no position grouping, so there's no real football-role reason for its weight to vary by position - the spread it used to have (0.12/0.14/0.16/0.20 for Attack/Midfield/Defender/Goalkeeper) was leftover perf_level weight parked somewhere convenient, now moved into rating/attacking/defensive/possession (the same FotMob components as permanent transfers - see compute_fotmob_component_pcts in build_dataset.py) instead, which is where it was already conceptually headed. Each FotMob component is only known for the loans FotMob has tenure stats for (scripts/fetch_fotmob_stats.py, same fetch as permanent transfers) - its weight is dropped and the rest renormalized for a loan missing it, same pattern as data/score_weights.json. Shared by scripts/build_dataset.py (computes the label) and app/main.py (labels the 'why this score' explanation). Each position row must sum to 1.0.
_sub_positions_comment: Sub-position weight overrides, same idea and same rows as data/score_weights.json's _sub_positions (see that file's comment for the full rationale) - a player's actual career-wide fielded sub-position selects one of these rows instead of the broad position row above when one exists; percentile ranking still groups by the broad position. value_growth is flat 0.12 here too, same as the broad rows above and for the same reason - it's a single global percentile rank with no position or sub-position grouping, so there's no football-role basis for it to vary at this level either; the offsetting weight moves into rating/defensive/possession instead. playing_time is left untouched throughout: whether a loan delivered game time isn't an attacking-vs-defending question.
